Trace the invoked command rather than assuming all builds use Turbo caching.

Continue with registration/context, validation, transports/adapters/uploads, client/workers, renderer, CLI, testing and release engineering. The Go map explains its explicit registration and native pipeline sites.

docs.title: Client SDK, React/RN and worker execution
docs.text: These are two different boundaries: client transport prepares a remote request; workers execute already-authorized server work. Neither is an authorization API.

docs.title: RpcClient and rawRpcRequest
docs.text:
packages/rpc-client/src/client.ts implements RpcClient, createRpcClient and rawRpcRequest. RpcClient resolves dynamic default headers/body, combines per-request settings and delegates. Plain object defaults are shallow merged; arrays/scalars/null keep shape rather than becoming object spreads. Undefined data can fall back to defaultBody or an empty object. These are SDK request-building semantics, distinct from the server's HTTP omission rule.

rawRpcRequest chooses a URL/rpcEndpoint, creates abort/timeout plumbing and sends an envelope for JSON. It parses the response status field, returns successful data and throws RpcError on RPC errors/parse/network failures. The word raw does not mean its return value is an HTTP envelope. User credentials belong in headers.

flowchart TD
  C["RpcClient defaults + request"] --> R["rawRpcRequest"]
  R --> K{"Multipart?"}
  K -->|No| J["JSON envelope via fetchFn"]
  K -->|Yes| F["buildRpcFormData + routing headers"]
  F --> X{"Native getParts FormData + XHR?"}
  X -->|Yes| H["sendMultipartXHR"]
  X -->|No| W["fetchFn with FormData"]
  J --> P["Parse RPC envelope / unwrap data / RpcError"]
  H --> P
  W --> P

docs.title: File serialization and real browser behavior
docs.text:
packages/rpc-client/src/multipart.ts detects Blob/File and RN URI objects, adds body routing first, preserves direct file arrays and maps reserved data keys namespace/functionName to _data_namespace/_data_functionName. Forbidden prototype keys are excluded. Nested file objects are rejected before transmission; ordinary nested JSON text is not a nested file transport feature.

Standard web FormData uses fetchFn even when XMLHttpRequest exists. Native bridge FormData exposes a callable getParts() consumed by React Native's networking bridge; that representation retains XHR when available, including forced text multipart, and does not invoke fetchFn. JSON and multipart without native XHR use fetchFn. This checks the constructed FormData representation rather than guessing the runtime from navigator.product or a Hermes global. A custom FormData polyfill must preserve the native bridge contract to use that compatibility path.

RN URI descriptors remain normalized as {uri,name,type}; this does not make them uploadable by ordinary browser FormData. File arrays and nested-file rejection are unchanged. Let the selected transport supply Content-Type/boundary. Browser custom fetch wrappers must forward the supplied headers, body and AbortSignal. The SDK has no upload-progress callback API; native XHR cancellation/error handlers remain unchanged. Full device/Hermes file I/O requires a native application test.

Client1.0.25 includes this correction;1.0.24 and older select XHR whenever it exists. See client transport configuration.

docs.title: React entrypoint
docs.text:
packages/rpc-client/src/react/context.tsx provides RpcProvider and useRpcClient. useRpcQuery manages enabled/data/header dependencies, in-flight identity/abort and refetch state; useRpcMutation manages mutate/loading/error/reset. Both take options objects. They are application conveniences, not a global cache, authorization boundary or idempotency system. React is optional for the base package; hooks are imported from @cellsweb/rpc-client/react.

The user client guide contains compiled TSX examples. React Native file descriptors are supported as described above, but documentation builds and Node/browser-shaped tests are not a real-device certificate.

docs.title: WorkerPool on the server
docs.text:
Source: packages/rpc-core/src/workers/worker-pool.ts. A top-level worker=true function export selects the pool in runPipeline, after middleware/function-header/input validation. The default pool size is bounded between2 and8 according to available CPUs. Tasks include module path, validated input, serializable context and an ID; the worker imports/caches the module and returns a result or error. The parent performs output validation.

sequenceDiagram
  participant P as runPipeline
  participant W as WorkerPool
  participant T as Worker thread
  P->>P: Auth and input validation
  P->>W: Enqueue validated task / serializable context
  W->>T: postMessage task
  T->>T: Import cached module / rehydrate file helpers
  T-->>W: Result or error
  W-->>P: Settle task
  P->>P: Output validation and response

Raw req/functions/AbortSignal are excluded from serialized context. File helpers are rehydrated around temporary paths; they are not transferred live sockets or arbitrary application instances. Do not assume structured cloning preserves every custom prototype. Parent timeouts reject waiting work; do not claim they forcibly cancel all CPU work or permit storing request temp files after cleanup.

CoreRPC.close owns framework server/pool shutdown, not arbitrary app timers or third-party resources. Test worker success/error/shutdown and file access while request ownership is valid. Declaration consumers and client multipart tests are separate gates; see testing.

docs.title: Node request execution lifecycle
docs.text: The entrypoint depends on the host; it is not the handler's responsibility to know whether the request arrived through native HTTP, Fetch or an in-memory call. Source: packages/rpc-core/src/core-rpc.ts, packages/rpc-core/src/interceptor.ts, packages/rpc-core/src/interceptor-web.ts and packages/rpc-core/src/pipeline.ts.

docs.title: Native HTTP / JSON sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant A as CoreRPC handler
  participant I as handleApiRequest
  participant P as parseRpcRequest
  participant M as runPipeline
  participant F as Function run
  C->>A: POST rpc endpoint
  A->>A: CORS and route selection
  A->>I: Request + loaded registry
  I->>P: Parse JSON envelope
  P-->>I: namespace, functionName, data
  I->>I: Build context / resolve function
  I->>M: key, input, headers, context
  M->>M: Middleware chain
  M->>M: Function headers + input validation
  M->>F: Validated input, trusted context
  F-->>M: Result
  M->>M: Output schema validation
  M-->>I: Data and metadata
  I-->>C: JSON success envelope
  I->>I: Finally: cleanup tracked temp paths

createHandler first loads/caches the registry, then returns the host callback. That callback unwraps req.raw/res.raw when present, handles OPTIONS/CORS, matches RPC, health and globally enabled docs routes, and delegates unknown paths to next or returns404. Docs/health do not invoke the RPC middleware pipeline.

handleApiRequest detects content kind, orchestrates parsing and builds context. JSON parsing validates the outer envelope/routing and preserves data shapes. Missing functions or wrong content contracts fail before handler invocation. runPipeline resolves the function and normally calls executeMiddlewareChain.

The chain prepares case-compatible schema headers, validates each middleware's headers/options, and runs attachments in order. A returned object becomes current context. Then function headers and input are validated, an aborted signal is checked, and the handler runs on the main thread or worker pool with a timeout. Output schema failure becomes schema_mismatch rather than a successful response. Timeout rejection is not a promise of forcibly cancelling arbitrary handler code.

docs.title: Multipart changes the placement of authorization
docs.text:
With paired routing headers, the interceptor resolves the function and runs its middleware before parser file writes. With body routing, onBeforeFileSave obtains the required early routing fields and runs the same chain. A cached pre-auth promise prevents concurrent file events from executing it repeatedly. After parsing, redundant header/body routing is checked before the handler.

runPipeline receives the internal skipMiddlewares marker only because that chain already ran during intake. It still validates function headers/input and output. The marker is not a remote request option and must not become an auth bypass. Parser failures clean partially created files; successful parse results transfer cleanup paths to the interceptor's finally block.

docs.title: Fetch and in-memory paths
docs.text:
CoreRPC.fetch parses a URL and gives its pathname to the docs renderer. RPC requests go through handleWebRpcRequest and parseWebRequest, then the same runPipeline. Fetch formData() may buffer before files are inspected; its pre-file callback protects application-owned writes, not runtime/network buffering.

CoreRPC.execute builds an in-process context and calls runPipeline directly, without an HTTP envelope parser. It returns a success/error envelope. Local contextOverrides are trusted server API inputs, not body fields accepted from HTTP clients. Do not apply HTTP omission defaults to this path by assumption.

docs.title: Error and resource ownership
docs.text:
Interceptors catch exceptions with toAppError, project AppError.toClientPayload, serialize safely and select HTTP200 unless useHttpStatusCodes is enabled. Telemetry callback failures are contained. Transport/framework failures occurring outside these wrappers may have different statuses. Cleanup runs in finally even when schemas, middleware, handlers or output validation fail. Disconnected peers may make a structured response impossible; draining remains bounded.

To extend intake, change the relevant parser and both transport wrappers only as needed. To change execution, start in pipeline.ts and verify native/Fetch/execute, pre-auth deduplication and output failures. See the test map.

docs.title: Shared protocol and compatibility boundaries
docs.text: This is a contributor description of the released behavior, not a new wire specification. Use it with the sibling runtime's source and equivalent fixtures. Node and Go share semantic contracts while retaining different native APIs, parsers, schema vocabularies and response details.

docs.title: HTTP envelope
docs.text:
A configurable endpoint (normally POST /rpc) receives an object with namespace, functionName and data. The outer JSON value is an envelope object; the data member may be an object, array, string, number, boolean or null if its schema accepts it. Omitted HTTP data retains the empty-object default; explicit null must reach schema validation as null/nil. Do not conflate envelope shape with handler-input shape.

{"namespace":"public","functionName":"hello","data":{"name":"Ada"}}

Success normally carries status:"ok", data and optional metadata. Some Go paths omit nil output data under existing omitempty rules; explicit null input is a separate guarantee. Errors have status:"error", code, message and optional details/metadata. Successfully handled application errors use HTTP200 by default, with explicit opt-in HTTP status mapping. Framework/server framing errors, custom routes and unmatched paths may instead use transport statuses or different non-RPC bodies.

Both interceptors in Node and sendErrorResponse in Go send their handled parsing errors through the default HTTP200 path too. Do not claim all malformed JSON, routing conflicts or missing boundaries automatically become HTTP400. Inspect which layer produced the failure, plus its configuration. Clients inspect the RPC status field instead of treating HTTP200 alone as success.

docs.title: Authentication, context and docs
docs.text:
Application middleware verifies credentials and authorization, in attachment order, before the handler. Missing configured middleware fails closed. HTTP/IPC callers forward headers; body/session/context objects remain untrusted data. Server-local test/context APIs are not remote bypass controls.

isPublic/IsPublic are deprecated ignored compatibility fields. They neither register/hide functions nor bypass authorization. No replacement visibility flag exists. Documentation is enabled/disabled globally. Middleware docs project structural schemas, descriptions and required headers, not resolved secret values. Never place secrets in public prose, names or schema constraints.

docs.title: Multipart is a transport, not a second business API
docs.text:
The client emits namespace/functionName text parts before files and also sends X-CRPC-Namespace/X-CRPC-Function. Header routing is an acceleration; required body routing is redundant and must agree. Headers come as a pair. Reject duplicates and conflicts rather than selecting an arbitrary source. Headerless fallback requires routing fields before file parts. Required authorization precedes application-owned file writes; this does not imply zero socket/runtime buffering.

File inputs are top-level fields or direct arrays of files. Nested files inside objects are not supported by the shared client transport. Ordinary nested JSON is separate. Text fields may be schema-coerced during multipart intake; ordinary JSON does not receive blanket transport coercion. Preserve parser/schema bounds, abort handling and temporary-file ownership.

docs.title: Shared intent and deliberate differences
docs.text:
Boundary Contributor implication Node discovery / Go registration Do not add filesystem discovery to Go to mimic Node. TypeBox / native SchemaRule Compare logical valid/invalid cases, not schema syntax. Optional/null/default semantics are not universally identical. Native Node / Fetch / Go HTTP Stream-driven Busboy, runtime-buffered formData, and transport-buffered fasthttp have different resource bounds. HTTP / in-memory / IPC HTTP omission defaults are not a promise about missing input on every call API. Return types and error/details/meta differ. Unix / stdio IPC Both bound line frames to 2,097,152 bytes including delimiters. Unix additionally accepts length-prefixed requests; stdio retains Scanner's final-EOF-line behavior. Browser / RN / Node client Client1.0.25 web FormData uses fetchFn; native getParts-compatible FormData retains XHR when available. Earlier clients select XHR whenever present.

Large integers, JSON duplicate members, extra properties, null outputs/omitempty, Unicode limits, details fields and cancellation need explicit fixtures when changed. Do not infer universal JSON Schema or byte-for-byte response parity. For protocol changes, propose version/migration behavior first and test both runtimes and every affected transport before seeking review.

See Node internals and Go internals.

docs.title: Function discovery, middleware and context
docs.text: Source: packages/rpc-core/src/registry.ts and packages/rpc-core/src/context.ts. Discovery executes module imports; it is not a schema-only filesystem index. Keep import side effects intentional.

docs.title: Registry lifetime and directory conventions
docs.text:
CoreRPC.getRegistry lazily calls buildRegistry and caches the result per app. buildRegistry scans central middleware first, then functions, with tinyglobby's **/run.{ts,js} pattern. Constants/attachment companion files can be ts/js/mjs; that does not make run.mjs a discovered entrypoint. Native Node without a detected TS runner probes compiled dist/.crpc directories; this heuristic is implemented in registry.ts, not an import resolver guarantee for arbitrary layouts.

A function needs a namespace directory and a function directory. The path relative to functionsDir supplies the namespace segments joined with dots, functionName is the final directory, and the key is namespace.functionName. Middleware names come from metadata.name or the directory basename. Central middleware holds its run function plus header/options schemas and description.

flowchart TD
  D["Configured directories / compiled fallback"] --> M["Import middleware run + constants"]
  M --> F["Import function run + constants + middlewares"]
  F --> K["Derive namespace.functionName"]
  K --> R["Registry Maps"]
  R --> P["Pipeline dispatch"]
  R --> V["Docs structural projection"]

docs.title: Module precedence
docs.text:
Function run is the named run export, a default function, or default.run. The run module's metadata/contentType/header/input/output exports take precedence over constants. worker is a top-level export of run or constants; setting metadata.worker alone does not activate worker execution. Middleware attachments are read from middlewares.ts/js/mjs first, then supported run/constants fallbacks. Use the documented co-located files instead of relying on unusual fallbacks.

Strict mode defaults on in production and propagates import failures; development can log/skip broken modules. A function that fails to register cannot be executed. A declared middleware missing at execution fails closed in the pipeline. Changes to discovery need tests for imported exports, invalid modules, namespace paths, compiled layout and actual generated apps. Filesystem access is a Node/Bun requirement; a Fetch-shaped API does not imply arbitrary Edge discovery support.

docs.title: Middleware context
docs.text:
executeMiddlewareChain receives headers, validated configured options, function metadata and current MiddlewareContext. It validates middleware headers before options, then invokes run. Attachments are ordered; context returned by one is passed onward. Keep state namespaced by middleware name to avoid collisions. The context includes requestId, ip, namespace, functionName, requestStartTime, request reference and optional signal. Headers/IP are transport input; proxy trust must be deliberate and an address is not an authenticated identity.

Application middleware must verify credentials and establish trusted state. The framework is not a JWT/session provider. Function headers/input are checked later by runPipeline. Server-local contextOverrides/test helpers are not remote HTTP/IPC options. Worker context is serialized differently; see client/workers. Avoid handler dependence on raw req/socket when it must also run through Fetch or in-memory execution.

docs.title: Safe changes
docs.text: Adding optional documentation metadata should not alter middleware execution. Keep isPublic ignored and retain source compatibility. Verify import/export precedence before adding generator fields. Tests in core-rpc.test.ts and security-hardening.test.ts plus generated-project suites exercise these paths; the test map links the exact locations.

docs.title: Release engineering and compatibility review
docs.text: Current documentation patch versions are Node core1.0.35/client1.0.26/scaffolder1.0.31, with runtime code/exports/dependencies unchanged from core1.0.34/client1.0.25/scaffolder1.0.30. Go module/CLI remains v1.0.2. The earlier client1.0.25 and Go v1.0.2 corrections are already publicly released; they must not be described as unpublished. Contributing a PR does not authorize pushing, tagging or publishing. Every release still requires author approval, validation and actual public-registry verification.

docs.title: Version and artifact boundaries
docs.text:
Node has three public npm workspaces plus a private root. Core runtime/helpers, client/React exports and the initializer have separate versions. Generated Node apps currently require core^1.0.34, so a new scaffolder must never require a core version that has not been published. Check actual registry state, not just local package manifests or a changed version string. Stable ranges do not select an unrelated prerelease; prerelease testing needs explicit versions/ranges/dist-tags.

Go is one root module, github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go. Root tags select both SDK and cmd/crpc-go; no separate invented CLI tag is needed. An installed versioned CLI uses its module version for the generated dependency. Source/VCS builds still use the real older v1.0.0 fallback; select a local SDK explicitly with a workspace. A CLI printing1.0.2 is not by itself evidence of generated SDK selection.

docs.title: Review and integration gates
docs.text:
• Agree scope/version/migration policy before changing public APIs, defaults or wire behavior. Preserve the shared invariants and test both runtimes when affected.
  • Record baseline/new SHAs and exact red/green commands. Run runtime-specific full builds/tests/typechecks/vet/race and real adapter/IPC tests where applicable.
  • Review docs examples, configuration precedence, ignored legacy metadata, error envelopes and resource ownership. Test actual package declarations/executables.
  • Use a clean worktree to preserve unrelated edits. Refresh default/upstream refs, confirm ancestry and integrate only the approved commit. Never force history or overwrite a published version/tag to rescue a failed release.

docs.title: Distribution sequence
docs.text:
1. After explicit release approval, recheck registry/tag absence, credentials, package names, engines/dependencies/exports/bins and exact artifacts. npm pack --dry-run and an inspected actual pack are separate from publishing.
  2. Publish the new core before any scaffolder requiring its new range, and publish the client at its own approved version. Use the official public registry and required public access. Prefer browser authentication; the maintainer completes passkey/2FA personally. Never ask for credentials in a PR or report.
  3. Create the approved new Go root-module tag at the verified commit; check the public proxy/checksum database before advertising its matching CLI/SDK install. Keep one publishing operation at a time and inspect each actual result.
  4. Repeat real installs in independent projects with fresh public caches and no local SDK links/replacements/workspaces/tarball overrides. Generate with npm create cellsweb-rpc-api@latest or a pinned initializer; build/typecheck/test and send actual JSON/multipart/error/docs HTTP requests on all seven adapters.
  5. Install the exact public Go CLI, generate an app, verify its go.mod and go list -m version, build/test/run HTTP and check IPC with the maintained Node client. Do not silently fall back to older code when propagation is delayed.
  6. Record published versions, integrity/module sums, remote SHAs/tag target and actual public-install results. Only then describe distribution as complete.

Both existing GitHub Pages workflows deploy docs on relevant main pushes. Review that timing and published-status prose; changing MkDocs source does not update an already-published immutable npm tarball's bundled README. No CI/workflow changes are implied by this guide. User installation examples are in getting started; migration keeps useful history from v1.0.0/older npm versions without calling released artifacts unpublished.

docs.title: Embedded documentation renderer
docs.text: The framework's interactive /docs is separate from this MkDocs contributor site. Source: packages/rpc-core/src/docs/renderer.ts, with routing in packages/rpc-core/src/core-rpc.ts.

docs.title: Input, views and routing
docs.text:
CoreRPC loads the registry and globally gates documentation before calling renderDocsHtml(registry, serverUrl, pathname, rpcEndpoint, docsEndpoint). Native HTTP passes its relative URL; Fetch passes parsed URL.pathname. The renderer normalizes the configured docs path, strips query/trailing slash syntax, resolves function or middleware details and falls back to the index for unknown documentation paths. The caller's docs switch determines accessibility; renderer classification is not authorization.

buildSidebar, renderDocsIndex, renderFunctionDoc and renderMiddlewareDoc use the same registry. Details include input/output contracts, function middleware, options/header structures, descriptions, required headers and placeholder cURL. Custom documentation and RPC endpoints must propagate through every link/example. Do not hard-code /docs when an endpoint parameter exists.

docs.title: Public projection versus live options
docs.text:
middlewareSchemaForDocs recursively projects schema structure and drops value annotations such as default/example/const/enum and private extensions. It does not read resolved per-function middleware option values. Required lists drive required-header display and cURL placeholders. Projection must not mutate schema objects or execute middleware/handlers. Keep descriptions/names free of secrets; no renderer can detect secrets deliberately embedded in public prose/constraints. Function input/output schema rendering has its own contract and is not a blanket redaction promise for arbitrary application metadata.

isPublic remains a deprecated ignored field. There are no PUBLIC/PRIVATE badges, per-function visibility opt-outs or auth bypasses. All registered functions may appear when docs are enabled. Node raw-core defaults and generated env parsing are described in the public configuration guide; do not silently change global switches while editing HTML.

docs.title: Safe renderer changes
docs.text:
1. Trace index/sidebar/search/directory and direct detail paths for the feature.
  2. Assert actual page content, input/output trees and per-function middleware.
  3. Test custom endpoints/query parameters/unknown routes and Node/Fetch parity.
  4. Test docs disabled: index/details/schema-like/metadata paths must not expose docs.
  5. Inject configured/schema secrets in fixtures and verify public views do not reveal them; also verify schemas and application execution are unchanged.
  6. Test deprecated metadata true/false/omitted without affecting visibility.

packages/rpc-core/src/docs-parity.test.ts checks safe projections and behavior; packages/rpc-core/src/fetch-docs.test.ts checks URL routing/content and HTTP/Fetch parity. Generated adapter probes cover the complete app boundary. A successful MkDocs build does not exercise this runtime renderer. See Go renderer internals for its native schema projection and intentionally different unknown-route behavior.

docs.title: Node tests and safe subsystem changes
docs.text: A test should reproduce behavior at the layer that owns it. Parser mocks alone cannot establish socket behavior; source imports alone cannot establish packed exports; HTTP200 alone cannot establish a correct RPC or documentation response.

docs.title: Source-to-test map
docs.text:
Change Tests / real path What to assert Registry/pipeline/errors packages/rpc-core/src/core-rpc.test.ts, packages/rpc-core/src/framework-integration.test.ts Imported functions, middleware order, missing middleware, headers/input/output, execute/workers JSON limits/auth/headers packages/rpc-core/src/security-hardening.test.ts Real HTTP oversized/slow/aborted bodies, error envelope, handler non-execution, cleanup/listeners Custom schema/nullable/file unions packages/rpc-core/src/union-validation.test.ts Positive/negative shapes, optional/null/defaults/transforms, physical file identity/limits Native multipart lifecycle packages/rpc-core/src/multipart-lifecycle.test.ts complete/readableEnded/end/close/aborted distinctions, temp cleanup Fetch body semantics packages/rpc-core/src/web-standards.test.ts Web Request/formData limits, routing/auth-before-write, files and JSON Documentation packages/rpc-core/src/fetch-docs.test.ts, packages/rpc-core/src/docs-parity.test.ts Actual detail/schema HTML, URLs/custom paths, disabled docs, ignored metadata, secret projection Client transport/form data packages/rpc-client/src/client.test.ts, packages/rpc-client/src/multipart.test.ts JSON shapes, default merging, RPC errors, routing fields, file arrays/RN/nesting rejection Fastify integration packages/create-cellsweb-rpc-api/test/fastify-multipart.test.mjs No415 before CRPC, existing parser, raw stream, JSON/route non-regression Seven generated projects packages/create-cellsweb-rpc-api/test/server-types.test.mjs, packages/create-cellsweb-rpc-api/test/server-docs.test.mjs, packages/create-cellsweb-rpc-api/test/multipart-adapters.test.mjs Actual tsc/build/HTTP and environment modes, not only text/200 Published declaration graph packages/rpc-core/test/consumer-types.mts, packages/rpc-core/test/consumer-types.cts Strict ESM/CJS helper composition, inferred input, legacy metadata/default import

The generated-project support files are packages/create-cellsweb-rpc-api/test/support/generated-project.mjs, adapter-probe.mjs, docs-probe.mjs and multipart-probe.mjs in the same directory. Workspace dependency links make normal regression runs practical; they are not a substitute for separate registry-only release validation.

docs.title: Executed commands versus claims
docs.text:
pnpm --filter @cellsweb/rpc-core exec vitest run src/union-validation.test.ts
pnpm --filter @cellsweb/rpc-client test
pnpm --filter create-cellsweb-rpc-api test
pnpm build
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm --filter @cellsweb/rpc-core test:types

The full Node release baseline reported364 runner entries (parent groups count in the Node test runner), not364 distinct Vitest leaf tests. Prefer fresh command results to stale counts. All seven adapters require real dependencies and Bun; state missing tooling instead of silently skipping. test:types needs registry access and runs an actual npm pack/install with fresh consumer dependencies.

docs.title: Red/green workflow
docs.text:
1. Pin baseline SHA and inspect the real owning function/adapter.
  2. Add a failure that captures user-visible behavior, including call counts and resource ownership. Run it before the fix and retain the failure output.
  3. Make the smallest implementation change for that root cause, respecting the protocol boundaries. Do not weaken validation/auth/limits.
  4. Run the focused regression then relevant existing suites. Broaden to full build/typecheck/tests for execution, parser, generator or export changes.
  5. For shared behavior, use equivalent inputs in Go's checked-in HTTP JSON fixture set and relevant transport suites. The review kit's parity driver is not a distributed contributor command; provide a reproducible harness/results.

Docs-only edits require strict site/link/diagram checks and meaningful executable examples, not synthetic tests mirroring prose. Do not refactor a pipeline, change XHR selection, add CI or change a frame limit as a side effect of documenting it.

docs.title: Node CLI, scaffolder and declaration build
docs.text: The initializer and runtime CLI are different responsibilities even though the released packages both expose a crpc binary. These internals describe the current layout; they do not remove or rename either executable.

docs.title: Project initializer
docs.text:
packages/create-cellsweb-rpc-api/bin/create.js parses interactive or flag-driven project/framework choices, copies template content, selects a server from templates/servers, writes the project manifest/tsconfig/scripts and optionally installs dependencies. The generated core range is ^1.0.34 and the Node engine range is >=24.0.0. Published user setup requires no local SDK link.

The template tree owns env parsing, sample functions/middleware, application telemetry/storage helpers, tests and Vitest configuration. Server variants own framework mounting and static-file response handling. These are application sources, not additional core RPC protocol endpoints. A template test must build and run the actual generated project; a matching string in a template alone cannot detect TypeScript export inference or BodyInit integration errors.

Application utilities live in template/src/utils/storage.ts, imageHandler.ts and telemetry.ts. They own persistence/URL helpers, image-field replacement and application metrics integration. Core owns request-temp intake, not the app's permanent storage or third-party telemetry lifecycle. Do not infer a real cloud provider was exercised from an SDK build; configure and test that integration separately.

docs.title: Runtime crpc command
docs.text:
packages/rpc-core/bin/crpc.js dispatches dev/build/start/test and function/middleware generation. Dev resolves an entry and chooses a Node TS runner or native Bun based on the CLI runtime; build invokes tsc and tsc-alias with extension rewriting; start runs emitted production JavaScript. The generated app supplies its build/test tools. The same-named initializer package CLI exists in the current release; use the app-local core command rather than global bin ordering assumptions.

Function/middleware generator modules are under the same bin directory. They support the documented flags and batch/file inputs. Programmatic scaffold helpers live in packages/rpc-core/src/scaffold.ts; do not assume every CLI flag or source-generation path is identical to that API. Add tests to the path actually changed. New functions should not generate ignored isPublic metadata.

docs.title: Environment and documentation defaults
docs.text: Generated src/env.ts imports dotenv without replacing existing exports and parses boolean/numeric values. Every server applies the established docs expression: outside production enabled; in production require parsed API_DOCS_ENABLED=true. An explicit application docs:false overrides this because it is application code. CoreRPC itself does not load dotenv; raw production environment defaults require the exact string true. Keep these existing precedence differences documented, not silently harmonized in a generator cleanup. Go's exported DOCS_ENABLED/ DOCS_PATH setup is a different API; see its contributor guide.

docs.title: Build/pack boundary
docs.text:
packages/rpc-core/package.json exposes one CommonJS JavaScript entry and module-mode-specific TypeScript declarations. tsc generates .d.ts; emit-import-types.mjs generates the .d.mts graph. test-types.mjs installs an actual pack into a strict clean consumer. The client has separate base/React exports; its package file filter excludes emitted test artifacts. The scaffolder must retain its intended template tests, not accidentally exclude all test.ts files.

To change CLI or package documentation, test --help/actual generation outside the monorepo, typecheck/build/run and check the packed file list/bins. Never change package versions merely to validate docs. Use testing and release engineering before proposing a distribution change.

docs.title: JSON, multipart and seven adapter boundaries
docs.text: Source entrypoints: packages/rpc-core/src/request/index.ts, packages/rpc-core/src/request/json.ts, packages/rpc-core/src/request/multipart.ts and packages/rpc-core/src/request/web.ts.

docs.title: JSON ownership
docs.text:
parseJsonRequest accepts an adapter-preparsed object, supported raw body data, or the native request stream. It validates the envelope object and routing; explicit data:null stays null, omitted data becomes an empty object. If another framework already buffered/parsed the body, its intake limit remains important. The native stream default is1,048,576 bytes (MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES overrides it).

On an oversized native body, normal chunk listeners are removed and accumulated chunks released. Rejection draining is bounded by512KiB additional bytes and a 2-second deadline, with request/socket/timer listeners cleaned up. It preserves an RPC error where the connection can still be used; it is not a promise of a response to an unlimited/slow/disconnected peer. Test actual HTTP, not just a synthetic parser object, when changing this lifecycle.

docs.title: Multipart intake sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant I as Interceptor
  participant M as Middleware chain
  participant P as Multipart parser
  participant D as Temporary storage
  participant F as runPipeline
  I->>I: Resolve paired header route when present
  opt Header route present
    I->>M: Authorize before body/file intake
  end
  I->>P: Parse with onBeforeFileSave callback
  opt Headerless body routing
    P->>I: Early routing fields before first file
    I->>M: Authorize once
  end
  P->>D: Create/write allowed temporary files
  P-->>I: Fields, files, cleanup paths
  I->>I: Require redundant routing consistency
  I->>F: Validate input, execute, validate output
  I->>D: Finally unlink temporary files

Busboy's native limits are20 files,100 fields,150 parts and1MiB per field. Default payload/file bounds are25,000,000 and10,000,000 bytes, controlled by MAX_MULTIPART_BYTES/MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_BYTES or applicable parser options. Parser accounting and a whole network request's byte count are not interchangeable. UPLOAD_TMP_DIR selects the application temp directory (default OS temp plus cellsweb-uploads); newly created directories/files request0700/0600 permissions. Filenames are sanitized; MIME detection is heuristic, not malware sanitization.

Native multipart pauses intake around authorization, streams file chunks to disk, tracks writes and cleans partial files on error. Successful paths transfer cleanup ownership to the interceptor. close is not always an abort: completion uses native complete when available and readableEnded otherwise, needed by Ultimate Express. Abort paths destroy/retire streams, bound draining and detach listeners. Do not remove these distinctions to make a happy-path upload pass.

Fetch uses request.formData(), which can buffer in the runtime before size/part checks. parseWebRequest then checks fields/files, runs the pre-save callback and creates physical UploadedFile values. Header authorization can occur before formData; headerless authorization occurs after form parsing but before application-owned file writes. This boundary cannot promise zero RAM or network backpressure equivalent to Busboy.

docs.title: Actual adapter map
docs.text:
Host Released template/integration Body ownership Native Node server.node.ts / createHandler IncomingMessage → Busboy/JSON stream Express server.express.ts / createHandler Host handles JSON; keep multipart raw for CRPC Ultimate Express server.ultimate-express.ts / createHandler Native-style stream with different completion properties Fastify server.fastify.ts / createFastifyPlugin JSON parser is upstream; multipart pass-through parser leaves payload unconsumed Bun server.bun.ts / fetch Request/Response/formData runtime boundary Elysia server.elysia.ts / Fetch integration Disable conflicting host body consumption; use Web intake Hono server.hono.ts / Fetch integration Web intake; tested Node host uses @hono/node-server

Templates are under packages/create-cellsweb-rpc-api/templates/servers. Fastify's plugin registers its non-consuming multipart parser only when absent; existing parser behavior remains the integrator's responsibility. Route handlers hijack the reply and use native request/response objects. Do not register a parser that drains the multipart payload before Busboy. Keep host JSON limits/config and custom endpoints in compatibility tests.

docs.title: Persistence and regression scope
docs.text:
UploadedFile exposes path/filename/byteLength/MIME properties and read methods. Persist to application-owned storage during handling; cleanup can remove the temp path after the response. Reading toBuffer/toBlob allocates content by choice. Do not retain temporary paths for asynchronous work after request completion.

Use real HTTP file arrays, empty files, all byte values, malformed boundaries, oversized/partial/slow/disconnected uploads and repeated requests. Assert routing mismatch rejection, auth-before-write, listener/timer cleanup and absence of temp files. The test map links lifecycle and seven-adapter probes.

docs.title: TypeBox validation and error projection
docs.text: Source: packages/rpc-core/src/utils/typebox.ts, packages/rpc-core/src/errors.ts and packages/rpc-core/src/utils/json.ts.

docs.title: What validates, and when
docs.text:
Boundary Owner Failure prevents Outer JSON object/routing identifiers request/json.ts and request/routing.ts Function lookup/dispatch Middleware headers/options executeMiddlewareChain That middleware and subsequent handler Function headers/input runPipeline Handler execution File identity/MIME/size/count validateSchema and registered file checks Invalid upload reaching handler Output schema runPipeline after handler Success envelope with invalid output Envelope serialization Interceptor/safeJsonStringify An unhandled serialization exception

TypeBox schemas are runtime objects carrying symbols, constraints/defaults and transforms. validateSchema caches a normalized safe schema/checker per schema. Normalization preserves every anyOf/allOf branch and nested items/properties. An unconditional Type.Any branch would widen a union; do not add one to make custom file types compile. Type.Optional concerns omission; explicit nullable values need a declared null branch. Existing schema defaults/transforms apply through the TypeBox path and must not mutate the contract object.

docs.title: File and form kinds
docs.text:
File/Files schemas retain custom kinds registered with TypeRegistry. Branch checks call validateFileField, preserving actual UploadedFile identity, limits, MIME rules and arrays. Multiple file alternatives must be tried as alternatives, not by choosing the first file schema. File-bearing default selection preserves opaque UploadedFile instances instead of letting generic clones erase methods. Ordinary JSON defaults stay on TypeBox's native path.

FormNum/FormBool are explicit helper transforms. Normalization recognizes their union kinds and decoding must occur once. They are not permission to coerce all JSON strings/numbers globally. Multipart intake has its own schema-directed data normalization. Nested validation of native file values does not imply the client supports nested file-in-object transport.

docs.title: Error types and status selection
docs.text:
AppError carries code/message/details and whether the error is internal. toAppError converts other exceptions; toClientPayload projects the client-facing error. Input/header validation uses validation_error. A handler returning output that violates its contract becomes schema_mismatch. Keep internal diagnostics in server logs rather than exposing arbitrary exception details as public metadata.

The Node and Fetch interceptors catch handled errors, serialize an error envelope and use HTTP200 by default. useHttpStatusCodes invokes the explicit mapper. Unknown paths/OPTIONS/native parser rejections may be outside that RPC path; never write tests that infer error vocabulary from status alone. Telemetry gets the chosen code/duration, but failures in telemetry do not replace the RPC result.

docs.title: Type declarations are part of compatibility
docs.text: The runtime JavaScript is CommonJS. Conditional exports provide .d.ts for require and .d.mts for import so TypeBox's module-specific unique symbols match consumers. packages/rpc-core/scripts/emit-import-types.mjs emits the import graph after tsc; packages/rpc-core/scripts/test-types.mjs packs and installs a clean strict ESM/CJS consumer. Preserve relative declaration references and inferred Static types. Do not solve symbol mismatches with any/ts-ignore.

docs.text: packages/rpc-core/src/union-validation.test.ts covers nullable omission/wrong shapes, optional/nested unions, transforms/defaults, file branches, file arrays, identity and HTTP handler non-execution.
